stage1.heading: Stage 1: Sort genes and events into biological pathways
stage1.instructions: Drag each card into the pathway you think it belongs to. A few genes plausibly belong to more than one pathway — that ambiguity is intentional and reflects real biology, not a bug.

items.label: Receptor Y activation
items.explanation: A ligand-receptor binding event — the classic first step of receptor activation.

items.label: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation
items.explanation: ROS buildup is the defining feature of oxidative stress.

items.label: Glutathione (GSH) depletion
items.explanation: Loss of this antioxidant buffer is a hallmark of oxidative stress.

items.label: Lipid droplet accumulation
items.explanation: Excess lipid storage points directly to disrupted lipid metabolism.

items.label: Cyp2e1-like enzyme induction
items.explanation: This enzyme family metabolizes lipids but also generates ROS as a byproduct — a genuine two-pathway gene.

items.label: NF-kB-like transcription factor activation
items.explanation: This factor drives inflammatory gene expression, but depending on context can also promote or block cell death — genuinely ambiguous.

items.label: Caspase-3-like protease cleavage
items.explanation: Executioner-caspase cleavage is a defining step of programmed cell death.

items.label: Mitochondrial membrane permeabilization
items.explanation: This event commits a cell to death, but the failing mitochondria also leak additional ROS — another two-pathway event.

items.label: Housekeeping structural protein X
items.explanation: A stable structural protein with no specific role in any of these five pathways — a distractor.

stage2.heading: Stage 2: Build the mechanistic sequence
stage2.instructions: Arrange the cards into the order Exposure → Molecular Initiating Event → Cellular Response → Tissue Outcome. One card doesn't belong in this sequence at all.

items.label: Oral exposure to fictional Compound X
items.explanation: The starting point: an organism is exposed to the compound.

items.label: Compound X binds Receptor Y
items.explanation: The first molecular interaction that sets the mechanism in motion.

items.label: Receptor Y triggers an oxidative-stress cascade
items.explanation: The cell-level consequence of the initiating event.

items.label: An unrelated lab measurement taken the same week
items.explanation: Not part of this mechanistic chain at all — included as a distractor.
